mission: The galley. Sera sets down her fork with precision that is itself a warning. Torin puts reasonable hands on the table. Four positions surface — Sera's, Torin's, Kael's, and Ben's (absent). Ben tables the debate; Kael closes it with a line that no one has an answer to. Per D7 counter-current 1, a small specific beat: when Sera pivots toward Kael with an edged question, Torin smoothly intercepts — redirects the heat to himself without making the redirect visible as one. A costless kindness to Kael. Ben sees it, does not interpret it, files it.
why_now: The thinning in the previous scene pushed the underlying disagreement into the room. Proceed without naming the positions and the group fractures on the next Corridor stop instead of at a table.
conflict: Three irreconcilable readings of the same history. Sera treats the Weave as something sacred and the technique as a violation. Torin treats the Weave as structure and the technique as a tool. Kael treats both frameworks as institutional propaganda. Ben does not have a position, and that is the problem. Sera's pressure starts to fall on Kael; Torin quietly absorbs it.
turning_point: Kael speaks last, landing a single-sentence observation that reframes all three positions as equivalent institutional captivities. Nobody answers, because nobody has a good answer.
opening_hook: It starts over food. Torin says something about the technique that makes Sera put down her fork with precision that is itself a warning
closing_hook: Kael's closing observation lands after everyone else has committed — one sentence reframing the three positions as equivalent cages. Nobody answers. Because nobody has a good response
emotional_trajectory: Simmering tension -> heated philosophical collision -> uncomfortable silence

stakes.personal: Ben's worldview destabilising — the Force he was taught does not match the room he is standing in
stakes.interpersonal: The group's ideological fault lines exposed; Torin's counter-current protection of Kael registers for Ben without explaining itself
stakes.external: Their ability to act together depends on some resolution or at least coexistence

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cramped common area, everyone too close together
sensory_details: Food cooling on plates; Sera's diction sharpening; Torin's warmth thinning for the first time in front of all of them; Kael's voice flat and cutting; Desh watching from the galley like an intelligence analyst reading a room
action_beats: Sera puts down her fork with controlled precision when Torin raises the technique over their meal
Torin spreads his hands on the table — a gesture of measured reasonableness that makes his argument feel inevitable

Sera turns toward Kael with an edged question; Torin smoothly redirects the exchange back to himself before Kael has to answer. The redirect is not visible as one. Kael does not need it; Torin does it anyway
Kael speaks last, his words landing in the silence after everyone else has committed their positions
promises_planted: Three different Force traditions can work in concert (PP13)
notes: Veraine's position (Weave as disease) is present by absence — the missing fourth voice, audible in its shape around the three that speak. Kael's closing observation (the 'cages' framing) is the line readers should remember from this chapter — land it and leave. Per D7 counter-current 1: Torin's intercept of Sera's pressure on Kael is a real ambiguity, not misdirection. On the corruption trajectory, Torin would want Kael vulnerable (so he can later recruit Kael into the forbidden-technique camp); here he protects Kael at zero cost to himself. The beat must read as characterisation, not plot signal — Ben sees the redirect, does not interpret it, files it. Per D7 anti-pattern, narrator does not correct Ben's file-and-move-on; no 'Torin was protecting Kael for reasons Ben would only later understand' line. The reader holds the beat as live ambiguity. Per D3, the Weave is the shared referent; Sera may use 'the work', Torin 'the stitching', Kael 'the cloth' — in-character variants without breaking the shared referent. Per D4, the concept-vs-sensation rule holds — each position's weight registers through body-language (Sera's fork, Torin's hands, Kael's flat voice) not through labelled philosophical abstractions. Per R11, Ben's close-third does not internally synthesise all four positions into a framework. He is the one person at the table without a settled answer; the scene's value is that his not-knowing is visible through what he does not say, not through an interior monologue labelling his own destabilisation. Per R12, Torin's warmth is load-bearing across this scene even as it thins during the argument — the counter-current protection of Kael refreshes the warmth specimen at the beat's exit. Anti-patterns: no monologues; Torin's reasonableness must be genuinely compelling on the page, not a strawman; Sera's anger should register in posture and diction, not in a speech; the Torin-counter-current beat is not underlined. Primary anchor: Allston (ensemble dialogue architecture — five distinct voices at a small table); supporting anchor: Zahn (discipline of scene structure), Bujold (Ben's interior register of the redirect he sees without interpreting).
